label: Institution
name: Assyrian Democratic Organization
summary:
The Assyrian Democratic Organization (ADO, Syriac: ܡܛܟܣܬܐ ܕܝܡܩܪܛܝܬܐ ܐܬܘܪܝܬܐ, Mțaksyayto Demokratayto Atwroyto), founded in Syria in 1957 — is one of the oldest Assyrian political parties, representing the Assyrian Christian minority of Syria (and the broader Assyrian diaspora) in advocating for Assyrian cultural, linguistic, and political rights within the framework of a democratic, secular state. It has maintained its identity as an Assyrian national organization through Syria's various political convulsions including the Ba'ath Party's authoritarian rule and the Syrian Civil War.

The Assyrian Christians of Syria — primarily in the northeast (Jazira region, now including much of the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria/Rojava) — are remnants of the ancient Syriac-speaking Christian civilization that predates Islam in the Middle East. The Assyrian (also called Syriac or Aramean, with complex internal naming disputes) Christian communities speak modern Neo-Aramaic dialects descended from the language of Jesus of Nazareth and the ancient Near Eastern Christian tradition.

The ADO's position during the Syrian Civil War (2011-present) has been particularly complex: with the rise of the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria (AANES/Rojava), many Assyrian Christians in the northeast came under the Kurdish-led administration, and Assyrian institutions including the ADO had to navigate relationships with the AANES, the Syrian government, and various external powers. The ADO has generally supported the Rojava democratic experiment while maintaining Assyrian specific autonomy demands.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Assyrian Democratic Organization — representing the ancient Syriac-speaking Christian community of Syria for 65+ years through Ba'ath dictatorship and civil war — is historically significant as a monument to Assyrian Christian political resilience and the survival of one of the Middle East's most ancient Christian communities.
